title: Playing best with friends: Lesberg, Holley, Barnes, Pizzarelli, Ellis
summary: Leeman says he is getting better with age and names bassists and guitarists he loved working with, such as George Barnes, Bucky Pizzarelli and Herb Ellis.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, another beautiful thing in life was playing with -- now I've got small band playing under my finger, more or less, and I'm transpiring -- I know things that I couldn't play two years ago that I can play now. I am to a certain degree, getting better, I'm getting more proficient each year. When that comes to an end, I guess I'll just plod along. I get a little more tired -- but I can play better each year, something new comes along to me. If I'm playing with the right people; if I'm playing with my friends, it was just most important. You got to play with friends. I Jack Lesberg, Major Holley, loved to work with you -- and good musicians like George Barnes, God bless his soul, he's gone. He had a knack....

Of not getting in the way, like Eddie Condon, and there was Bucky Pizzarelli, a great guitarist, and I enjoyed working with him. And the epitome -- well, not the epitome, but one of the greats was from Texas, Herb Ellis.

And now Pete catches a little thing, and he gets a little style of his own -- but when you play with Herb Ellis, what gets me about him, is he's playing Basic amplified guitar, and he's playing at nine bra(s)
Well, we don't want to get into this kind of thing.
But these things are what make life beautiful.
